name: Pakistan
nickname: Sabz Hilali Parcham (the green crescent flag)
designer: Syed Amir-uddin Kedwaii, based on the All-India Muslim League flag
summary: A dark green field with a white crescent and five-pointed star, and a white vertical band at the hoist. Adopted by the Constituent Assembly three days before independence, it represents the Muslim majority and the country's religious minorities.
origin: The flag is based on that of the All-India Muslim League, a green flag with a white crescent and star used from 1906 in the campaign for a Muslim homeland. Syed Amir-uddin Kedwaii adapted it for the new state, adding a white band at the hoist.
The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947, three days before Pakistan's independence on 14 August.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Religious minorities. Liaquat Ali Khan told the Assembly the flag stood for all citizens, not a single community.

symbols.name: Crescent
symbols.description: A white crescent opening toward the upper fly.

symbols.name: Star
symbols.description: A white five-pointed star beside the crescent.

history.label: All-India Muslim League flag
history.note: Green with a white crescent and star.

facts: The white band occupies one quarter of the flag's length.
Flag Day ceremonies are held on 14 August, Independence Day.
Turkmenistan, Algeria and the Maldives also pair green with a white crescent, but Pakistan's is the only one with a white band at the hoist.
clues: Dark green with a white crescent and star, and a white band at the hoist.
Its white band represents religious minorities.
Adopted three days before its country became independent.
Based on the flag of a political party founded in 1906.
